claim: Perseverance found Mars dust grains fine enough to reach deep into human lungs if inhaled; Mars dust is also known to carry perchlorate salts that, in large doses, can disrupt the thyroid, so it could harm crews, depending on how much dust and for how long.

beats.caption: Apollo had a dust problem
beats.vo: Moon dust scratched Apollo visors. Some crew reported hay fever-like symptoms. Mars dust is less scratchy. The catch: size and chemistry.

beats.caption: Tiny grains, perchlorate salts
beats.vo: Spacesuit swatches on NASA's Perseverance rover collected grains hundreds of times thinner than a hair, small enough to reach deep into lungs if inhaled. Separately, Mars dust carries perchlorates, salts containing chlorine and oxygen. In large doses, they can disrupt your thyroid gland, whose hormones control your body's energy use.

beats.caption: Risk: how much, how long
beats.vo: So yes, it could, depending on how much dust and for how long. One idea: suits attached outside the habitat, so less dust could get in. How would you keep it out?
